ENet 1.3.13 (http://enet.bespin.org/download/enet-1.3.13.tar.gz, sha256
e36072021faa28731b08c15b1c3b5b91b911baf5f6abcc7fe4a6d425abada35c). Its source files are the same
bytes as tag v1.3.13 of https://github.com/lsalzman/enet (commit f7c46f03fd8d883ac2811948aa71c7623069d070).
Only the library: *.c, include/enet/*.h and LICENSE (MIT). Used by Slippi netplay (port/runtime/hle)
and the peer connector (port/runtime/mu_net).

Held at 1.3.13 on purpose. Slippi's Dolphin ships ENet 1.3.13, and this client talks to stock Slippi
clients and the Slippi matchmaking server. The packet format is the same in later 1.3.x releases.
What changed after 1.3.13 is how the sender schedules packets (reliable windows, throttle, RTT,
default MTU). Do not update without testing against stock Slippi.

This folder is upstream 1.3.13 plus melee-unlocked.patch, which only adds receive-side checks:
- protocol.c: each command's payload length is checked against the bytes left in the datagram
  before the read pointer moves (upstream moves the pointer first, then compares pointers). The
  header size, including the checksum, is checked before anything reads it. Empty or truncated
  datagrams are counted and shown to the intercept, but not parsed. offsetof replaces the
  null-pointer offset trick.
- win32.c, unix.c (enet_socket_receive): a truncated datagram returns ENET_SOCKET_RECEIVE_TRUNCATED
  and an empty one ENET_SOCKET_RECEIVE_EMPTY (both defined in enet.h), with the sender's address
  filled in. Upstream returns -1 for truncated datagrams, which makes enet_host_service fail.
  It returns 0 for empty ones, which ends that receive pass.
- unix.h, unix.c: socket descriptors at or above FD_SETSIZE are refused, instead of writing past
  the fd_set.
- peer.c, protocol.c, enet.h: receive-side fixes from later upstream releases, listed below.
Nothing on the send side changes, so what goes out on the wire is unchanged.

Backported from upstream (receive side only; the release is still 1.3.13 otherwise):
- 1.3.16, 259e5db and e55d226 ("queuing fix"): enet_peer_queue_incoming_command dispatches the
  channel's unreliable queue, which could free the command it had just queued and then return it.
  The fragment handlers wrote into that freed command. The dispatch functions and
  enet_peer_remove_incoming_commands now take the command just queued and leave it in place.
  enet_peer_dispatch_incoming_reliable_commands and enet_peer_dispatch_incoming_unreliable_commands
  gain that third argument (NULL from everywhere else), as upstream.
- 1.3.18, d7e5470 and 657eaf9: a reliable or unreliable fragment with no data, or a fragmented
  packet whose totalLength is smaller than its fragmentCount, is refused. Such a packet could be
  marked complete with none of its bytes written, so it was delivered holding uninitialised memory.
  ENet's own sender never sends either (every fragment carries at least one byte).
These were written to match the upstream commits named, without the upstream files at hand.
Compare them with those commits when this folder is next updated.

To check (Git Bash or another POSIX shell, from the repository root). It prints only the hash,
then nothing if the folder is upstream plus the patch. --strip-trailing-cr is there because a Windows
checkout has CRLF line endings; the repository stores LF.
  r=$PWD/port/third_party/enet; t=$(mktemp -d)
  curl -sSLo "$t/enet.tar.gz" http://enet.bespin.org/download/enet-1.3.13.tar.gz
  sha256sum "$t/enet.tar.gz"
  tar xzf "$t/enet.tar.gz" -C "$t" && cd "$t/enet-1.3.13" && patch -s -p1 < "$r/melee-unlocked.patch"
  (cd "$r" && find . -type f ! -name SOURCES.txt ! -name melee-unlocked.patch) | while read -r f; do
    diff -q --strip-trailing-cr "$f" "$r/$f" >/dev/null || echo "differs: $f"; done; cd - >/dev/null
To regenerate the patch after a deliberate change, diff the pristine files against this folder
(git diff --no-index --no-prefix a b, with a = pristine and b = this folder, minus these two files).
